title: Error by AI scribe during medical appointment leaves patient devastated

reports.title: Error by AI scribe during medical appointment leaves patient devastated

summary:
Rebecca Green agreed to let an artificial intelligence tool transcribe her first urologist appointment, but the software invented a claim that she took psychedelic mushrooms in small doses. She had never used the drug and only noticed the false statement after kidney stone surgery in March, when a postoperative letter to her GP repeated it. Ms Green, who was receiving workers' compensation, feared the error could harm her case. After she complained, the urologist apologised, corrected the record, and said she would review how AI was used in her practice.

A Digital Rights Watch report found similar AI scribe mistakes, including recording the wrong breast in a cancer diagnosis and inventing epilepsy. The Royal Australian College of GPs estimates 40 per cent of GPs regularly use these tools. Australia's medicines regulator, the TGA, is reviewing AI scribes and will release findings in coming weeks, with breaches to be acted upon. Patient advocates want approved tools tested by the new AI Safety Institute. Ms Green said she would only consent again with a doctor she already knew.
